gloss: carefree; having known no hardship; sheltered

definitions.gloss: carefree; having known no hardship; sheltered; inexperienced in difficulty
definitions.explanation: Describing someone who has grown up or lived without ever experiencing real struggle or hardship, often implying a privileged or sheltered upbringing.

examples.japanese: {苦労知|くろうし}らずに{育|そだ}った。
examples.english: I grew up without knowing hardship.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{苦労知|くろうし}らずのお{坊|ぼっ}ちゃんだ。
examples.english: He is a sheltered rich kid who has never known hardship.

examples.japanese: {苦労知|くろうし}らずだった{自分|じぶん}が、{社会|しゃかい}に{出|で}て{初|はじ}めて{大変|たいへん}さを{知|し}った。
examples.english: Having been sheltered, I learned for the first time how tough things are when I entered the real world.

notes:
A compound of {苦労|くろう} (hardship, difficulty) and {知|し}らず (not knowing). Describes someone who has been fortunate enough — or sheltered enough — to never experience real difficulty. The tone can be neutral (simply describing someone's fortunate upbringing) or slightly critical (implying naivety or a lack of empathy due to inexperience).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {苦労知|くろうし}らずに{育|そだ}つ: to grow up without hardship
- {苦労知|くろうし}らずの{人生|じんせい}: a life without hardship
- {苦労知|くろうし}らずのお{坊|ぼっ}ちゃん: sheltered rich boy

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {世間知|せけんし}らず: naive about the ways of the world — focuses on social inexperience
- のんき: carefree, easygoing — personality trait rather than life circumstance
- お{気楽|きらく}: carefree, happy-go-lucky — more colloquial and often slightly critical
